body:
DEFERRED OUT OF THE USERS/CONNECTORS ARC BY MYK, 2026-07-27. It is not a phase of that work.
Do not fold it into one.

WHAT MYK SETTLED, and it is the premise here rather than a question: "Any operator has equivalent
operator privilege over the whole store." There are no operator tiers. He also observed the consequence
himself: if a role assignment is just a delta, then anyone holding the operator role should be able to
issue one. That is the right END STATE.

WHAT THE ARC BUILDS INSTEAD, deliberately: role assignment is CLI-ONLY. The CLI signs with the store's
own seed at `<home>/operator.seed`. So the LIMIT IS THE TRANSPORT, not the privilege — every operator is
equally able to assign a role with home access, and equally unable to do it remotely.

WHY THE OBVIOUS SHORTCUT IS AN ESCALATION, measured. An independent review caught this in the plan's
first revision, where it had become an acceptance criterion. `src/server/users.ts` states it plainly: a
role binding "has no grant shape for `constitutionalDefect` to recognise and nothing refuses it at the
append door". So the READ-SIDE select is the only defence. Widen the role read from the store's seed to a
trust set and ANY member can append a role claim at `user:carol` granting `operator`, and the read admits
it. Stratification does not help: it bounds set MEMBERSHIP depth and says nothing about who may WRITE a
role.

SO THE REAL WORK IS AT THE APPEND DOOR. `constitutionalDefect` today recognises only `loam.grants`,
`loam.members` and `loam.tenant` shapes. A role binding at an ordinary entity in an ordinary context is
not among them, so nothing refuses it. This ticket adds the validation that makes a role binding a
recognised, refusable shape: a role claim is admitted only when its author holds the operator role
itself. Then, and only then, the read may widen.

A SECOND CONSTRAINT worth knowing before designing: an `inView` extract compares only `author` or `id`
(`@bombadil/rhizomatic/dist/pred.d.ts`). A role binding's pointers are an entity and a primitive, so a
trusted set cannot be built from role bindings directly. The GRANT vocabulary works because a grant's
`subject` is a primitive holding a public key. Any design here must say which delta carries the key.

AND A LIMIT THAT DOES NOT GO AWAY. The filesystem stays the trust root. Anyone who can read the store's
seed can sign anything, including a role binding for themselves. This ticket cannot change that and must
not claim to. It governs the REMOTE path only.

RAILS, and both directions are load-bearing:
  - an operator-role user CAN mint an operator remotely, and the new operator's role resolves;
  - a user WITHOUT the operator role CANNOT, and the attempted claim is refused AT THE APPEND DOOR
    rather than admitted and ignored on read. Assert at both levels: the delta is absent from the store,
    and no reading admits it.
  - revoking the minting operator's role does not retroactively unmake the operator they minted. State
    whichever answer the design picks and rail it; do not leave it to inference.

DESIGN-STAGE: it changes what the system PROMISES, so the working spec stops for Myk before any
implementation code, and the landing PR is his merge. It depends on the arc's phase 3 landing first,
because it generalises what phase 3 builds.
title: Any operator may mint an operator — the remote role-assignment path, and the append-door validation it needs
